title: Stop prompting Claude: files-as-prompts with Cowork + Obsidian as a "Second Brain"
summary: Ruben argues that one-line prompts give average, generic output because Claude lacks context. His fix is Claude Cowork pointed at a folder of text files (style, rules, goals) that act as a permanent prompt. He pairs it with Obsidian so non-developers can read, search and edit those files, and adds Skills for repeated tasks.

principles.text: Bad AI output usually comes from missing context, not a bad model; don't blame the tool.
principles.quote: You didn’t give Claude enough context. You didn’t explain your tone, your audience, your rules. Everything.

principles.text: Replace retyped prompts with saved files Claude reads every session: the files are the prompt, forever.
principles.quote: Claude reads them automatically before every session. **The files are the prompt. Forever.**

principles.text: Fix a recurring Claude annoyance once in your context file instead of re-correcting it in every chat.
principles.quote: You prompted Claude once, and it remembers forever. Literally your Second Brain.

principles.text: Pick tools by friction for non-technical users: free, local, clean, and they never alter your files.
principles.quote: I picked it because everything else failed at least one of my criteria.

principles.text: Turn tasks you repeat weekly into Skills (one file per task) callable with a slash command.
principles.quote: You say it once, fine. You say it 30 times, that’s not so efficient.

principles.text: Distribution runs on shares; make the content free and ask readers to pass it to someone helpful to them.
principles.quote: This newsletter mostly grows because of your shares. And I keep hitting 1,000+ shares. It’s my north star.
